Watcher
WOCH-er
noun
An angelic being who watches and executes God’s decree (Daniel 4:13, 17); from the wakeful, watching character of the heavenly host.

Biblical Definition

A watcher is an angelic being named in the visions of Daniel—a watcher and an holy one came down from heaven—who watches over the affairs of men and executes the decrees of the Most High. In Nebuchadnezzar’s dream, the felling of the great tree is pronounced by the decree of the watchers, the demand by the word of the holy ones, to the intent that the living may know that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men. The watchers are thus the wakeful servants of God’s providence, attending His throne, observing the doings of men, and carrying out His sentences upon kings and nations. Their name fittingly expresses a truth of the whole heavenly host and of God Himself: the eyes of the LORD are in every place, beholding the evil and the good; He that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep. Nothing escapes the wakeful watch of heaven; the proud king is humbled by the decree of the watchers, that he may learn who truly reigns. The dictionary reads the watcher as the figure of God’s sleepless oversight of the world—the angelic watcher executing the divine decree, and behind him the unsleeping God whose eyes run to and fro throughout the whole earth—a solemn warning to the proud that heaven watches and judges, and a comfort to the saint that the God who keeps him never slumbers nor sleeps.

Webster 1828 Definition

An angelic being of Daniel’s visions who watches over men and executes God’s decree; a figure of heaven’s sleepless oversight—warning to the proud, comfort to the saint whose Keeper never sleeps.

Key Scripture

Dan 4:13 — "I saw in the visions of my head upon my bed, and, behold, a watcher and an holy one came down from heaven;"

Dan 4:17 — "This matter is by the decree of the watchers, and the demand by the word of the holy ones: to the intent that the living may know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will, and setteth up over it the basest of men."

Pro 15:3 — "The eyes of the LORD are in every place, beholding the evil and the good."

Psa 121:4 — "Behold, he that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep."

Modern Corruption

Apocryphal and occult traditions spin the “watchers” into elaborate myths of fallen angelic origins; Scripture names them holy servants of God’s decree, figures of heaven’s sleepless oversight.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The corruption to name is the spinning of the “watchers” into elaborate myth. Apocryphal works such as 1 Enoch, and the occult and speculative traditions that feed on them, build whole mythologies of fallen “Watchers” who corrupted mankind—legends that have gripped imaginations but rest on no canonical foundation. The dictionary keeps to Scripture. In Daniel the watcher is a holy one, an angelic servant of the Most High who comes down from heaven to pronounce and execute God’s decree; he is no rogue or fallen being but an instrument of divine providence. The canon, not the apocrypha, governs what we believe of the watchers.

The principle to recover is the sleepless oversight of God over the world. The watcher of Daniel executes the decree of the Most High, that the living may know that He rules in the kingdom of men and sets up whom He will—humbling the proud Nebuchadnezzar until he learns who truly reigns. And the watcher’s name expresses a truth of God Himself: His eyes are in every place, beholding the evil and the good, and He that keeps His people neither slumbers nor sleeps. Heaven watches; nothing escapes its eye. This is a solemn warning to the proud, who imagine no one sees, and a deep comfort to the saint, whose Keeper is awake and watching over him through every night.
